e.meaning: of the Gauts, a Germanic people
e.etymology: A respelling of Jocelyn, from the Norman name Joscelin, a Germanic name referring to the Gauts, a Germanic people. Spanish-speaking families often favor the Jose- spellings.
A modern American name that joins the Ja- prefix to the sound of Amari and Maurice; compare Jamari and Jamarion.
Igbo chi oma: chi is God or a person's guardian spirit, and oma is good. The name gives thanks for good fortune and is very common among Igbo families in Nigeria.
In Icelandic, Lóa is a girls' name meaning golden plover, a bird that signals spring. In Hawaiian, loa means long, as in Mauna Loa. The source of its American use around 1900 is unclear.
e.note: Loa is also the usual English spelling for the spirits of Haitian Vodou.

e.etymology: A respelling of Jackson, an English and Scottish surname meaning son of Jack. Jack began as a medieval pet form of John.
A modern American name that reshapes Ryker with the -en ending of Aiden and Jaxen. Ryker itself comes from a Dutch or German surname.
A modern American name of the Jamir and Jahmir family, combining Jah- with the -mir sound of Amir, Arabic for prince.
A respelling of Amir, Arabic for prince or commander, from the root amara, to command. The word emir comes from the same source.
A modern American name on the pattern of Cordell and Corday with the -ae ending of Dontae and Davontae. Rapper Cordae, born Cordae Dunston in 1997, performs under his given name.
A spelling of Misael, the Spanish form of Mishael, Hebrew for who is what God is? In the Book of Daniel, Mishael is one of Daniel's three companions, renamed Meshach in Babylon.
A spelling of Mira, a name with several sources: Latin mirus, wonderful; the Slavic element mir, peace or world; and the Indian name Meera, after the 16th-century poet-saint Mirabai.
A spelling of Charisma, the English word for personal magnetism, from Greek kharisma, a gift of grace. The Kh follows the Greek letter chi.
An English surname of place-name origin, now used as a given name in the style of Clayton and Layton.
namesakes: Deke Slayton (one of NASA's original Mercury Seven astronauts)
e.note: Contains slay, a violent verb and also current slang for doing something very well.

e.etymology: An English nickname and word. Chipper means cheerful and lively, and as a nickname it extends Chip, as in a chip off the old block. Baseball Hall of Famer Chipper Jones made it familiar.
namesakes: Chipper Jones (Atlanta Braves Hall of Fame third baseman)

assoc.t: Chipper Jones, Atlanta Braves Hall of Famer

e.etymology: An Indian girls' name made widely known by badminton champion Saina Nehwal, an Olympic medalist and former world number one.
The Ashkenazi Hebrew pronunciation of Netanel, the original of Nathaniel: natan, he gave, and El, God. Used mainly in Orthodox Jewish communities.
A spelling of Eileen, the English form of Irish Eibhlín, which came from the Norman French name Aveline. This spelling is also used in Germany and Latin America.
A modern American blend of Anna and Aliyah, close to the older Spanish name Analía.
From Sanskrit amala, spotless or pure, formed from a-, without, and mala, stain. It is a familiar girls' name across India.
From the Semitic word for the right hand, yamin in both Arabic and Hebrew, a symbol of strength, good fortune and oaths. In the Bible Jamin is a son of Simeon.
A modern American name with the sound of Sia and of names ending in -siah, such as Josiah and Messiah.
A Bengali name borrowed from Sanskrit sayana. Sayana was also the 14th-century scholar whose commentaries on the Vedas are still standard.
e.note: Sounds close to Saiyan, the warrior race in the Dragon Ball anime.

e.etymology: A South Indian spelling of Tara, from Sanskrit tara, star, also the name of goddesses in Hindu and Buddhist tradition. Thara is separately an Arabic name meaning wealth.
In Dutch and Estonian, a short form of names beginning with Rein-, such as Reinier and Reinhard, from Germanic ragin, counsel. In the United States it is also used as a spelling of Rain or Reign.
A phonetic respelling of Cassius, a Roman family name of uncertain meaning, written the way many Americans say it. Cassius Clay was Muhammad Ali's birth name.
A modern American name that combines the sound of Layla or Leila with Lynn.
From Sanskrit manavi, belonging to humankind, the feminine of manava, human, a descendant of Manu, the first man in Hindu tradition. Often glossed as humane or kind-hearted.
The Spanish and Portuguese form of Apollo, the Greek god of the sun, music, poetry and prophecy. The origin of the god's name is uncertain.
namesakes: Apolo Ohno (Olympic short-track speed skating champion)

assoc.t: Apolo Ohno, Olympic speed skating champion

e.etymology: A respelling of Whitley, an English place name and surname from Old English hwit, white, and leah, a woodland clearing or meadow.
The name of the light-talent fairy in Disney's Tinker Bell films, coined from iridescent, which goes back to Greek iris, rainbow.
namesakes: Iridessa (light fairy in Disney's Tinker Bell films)

assoc.t: Iridessa, the light fairy of Disney's Tinker Bell films
